source_request: 시각 의미 데이터와 후보팩에 반영해줘. 시각 의미 데이터의 대체 표현을 추가/보강하는 작업을 중심으로 진행하고 후보팩에도 잘 반영해줘. 그 다음 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 반영한 키워드가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 랜덤한 복잡한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
interpreted_intent: The user asks for an independent random complex concept to test keyword realization and an attached-image-guided prompt/image. The agent, not the requester, randomly selected Greek siren and chimera from coordinator stimuli and chose a tactile modern museum animatronic encounter. Distinct connected silhouettes carry visual complexity without fusing creatures. Reference use supplies visible eye, face and bob-hair cues to an explicitly fictional adult siren, with no identity, age, religion, body, personality or consent inference.
subject: One human-headed avian Greek siren and one lion-goat-snake chimera, each a distinct continuous creature; these test selections and counts are agent-owned.
setting: A contemporary museum black-box kinetic diorama with a stage floor and black curtains.
event: A Greek siren perches with two wings open as her song pauses while a four-footed chimera faces her across clear floor, its goat head arising from its back and serpent tail extended visibly.
visual_priorities: The siren human neck enters the same feathered bird trunk that owns both wings and two taloned bird legs.
The chimera lion head, dorsal goat head and snake-tipped tail belong to one lion torso.
Two whole connected silhouettes face each other across an open floor gap.
Visible portrait face and bob-hair cues belong only to the fictional adult siren.
Tactile stage light makes feather, fur and scale surfaces legible.
baseline_prompt_en: Photograph a complex myth-creature tableau in a contemporary museum's black-box kinetic diorama, where composite myth creatures hold a suspended encounter with connected forms visible together. On the left, one Greek siren perches on a low stone block: an explicitly fictional adult female human head and neck join directly into one feather-covered bird trunk. Her two feathered wings attach to that trunk; both wings fan outward above her two scaly bird legs and gripping talons. Her dark brown eyes, soft oval face, straight short dark bob and wispy bangs take visible appearance cues from the attached portrait. She faces the camera with her mouth gently parted as if the song has just stopped. The bird's breast, wing roots, avian legs and feathered tail remain visible as parts of her continuous body. On the right, one chimera stands in three-quarter profile on four feline paws: its lion head and mane connect to a single tawny lion torso, a horned goat head and neck grow upward from the middle of that same back, and its long scaly tail continues from the rump into a distinct snake head. The serpent tail curves outward into the open right side of the stage, its root and entire course readable. The goat is a connected anatomical outgrowth. The two creatures face across a clear strip of floor, each body's contour separated from the other. A warm stage lamp illuminates the siren's human face and layered feathers; a cooler wash reveals the lion fur, goat neck and serpent scales. Photograph both entire creatures in one horizontal frame from modestly elevated chest height, keeping all body junctions, claws, paws and tail tips in focus. Black curtains and a worn stage floor give the fantastical pair the tactile presence of museum animatronics.
